{"self_assessment": "Impact: I started the build by fetching a full load of 40 dominoes for the shared bin, which the whole table drew on. I laid the start domino and traced stroke 1, the top line of the fish, which is the longest run and carries the fall out from the nose. I then carried the bottom line on into the tail flare at the lower right. That gave the fish its two-lobed tail, the feature that makes the outline read as a fish. By the eye trace, about 101 of the 108 standing dominoes were connected to the start for the push.

Execution: I took a clear piece of work, the start and top line followed by the bottom flare, and stuck with it from the first minute to the last. I worked in short bursts and inspected the flare area closely several times to check what was and wasn't catching. I then adjusted the join, using extend, standing dominoes back up and clearing strays. I used the bin well and didn't spend time on extra trips.

Collaboration: I agreed on the fish early and settled who took which stroke. I kept the table posted on where my hands were so we didn't bump each other. I took advice on the join from Sofia and Hana, adopting the gentler bend, and thanked people who helped, including Omar on the top tail. When Sofia took over the final join near the end, I handed it over and kept my hands off for the push.

Leadership: I took the top line and the flare, and I called out when I was working in a spot so others could stay clear. I kept the team's focus on a full check of the fall before time ran out. I also stepped back at the end so the join could be finished cleanly.", "my_share_percent": 30}
